equation_request.abstract: Quantum logic decomposition refers to decomposing a given quantum gate to a set of physically implementable gates. An approach has been presented to decompose arbitrary diagonal quantum gates to a set of multiplexed-rotation gates around $z$ axis. In this paper, a special class of diagonal quantum gates, namely diagonal Hermitian quantum gates, is considered and a new perspective to the decomposition problem with respect to decomposing these gates is presented. It is first shown that these gates can be decomposed to a set that solely consists of multiple-controlled $Z$ gates. Then a binary representation for the diagonal Hermitian gates is introduced. It is shown that the binary representations of multiple-controlled $Z$ gates form a basis for the vector space that is produced by the binary representations of all diagonal Hermitian quantum gates. Moreover, the problem of decomposing a given diagonal Hermitian gate is mapped to the problem of writing its binary representation in the specific basis mentioned above. Moreover, CZ gate is suggested to be the two-qubit gate in the decomposition library, instead of previously used CNOT gate. Experimental results show that the proposed approach can lead to circuits with lower costs in comparison with the previous ones. Keywords— Diagonal Hermitian quantum gates, Optimization, Decomposition

specification.problem: Decompose an n-qubit diagonal Hermitian gate into multiple-controlled Z gates by mapping the gate to a binary vector over GF(2) and expressing it in the basis given by binary representations of multiple-controlled Z gates.
specification.reconstruction_scope: Tiny instance: n=2 qubits. Diagonal Hermitian gate D=diag((-1)^{f(x)}) with f:{0,1}^2->{0,1}. Binary representation is the vector of f values; basis is the set of multiple-controlled Z gates (Z on qubit 1, Z on qubit 2, CZ). Out of scope: general n, cost optimization, CZ vs CNOT library cost comparison, experimental results, and the paper's exact binary representation and basis construction.

symbols.meaning: diagonal entry for basis state x
binary representation vector of D (assumed to be the f values)
subset of qubits acted on by a multiple-controlled Z gate
coefficient indicating whether MCZ_S is included

equations.label: Diagonal Hermitian form
equations.description: A diagonal gate is Hermitian and unitary iff its diagonal entries are real and of unit modulus, hence +-1.
equations.justification: D=D^dagger needs real entries and unitarity needs modulus 1, so entries are +-1. The abstract only says these gates can be decomposed into MCZ gates.
assumptions: Gate is both Hermitian and unitary

equations.label: Binary representation
equations.description: Assumed binary vector encoding of D, with x ordered as an integer with qubit 1 as most significant bit.
equations.justification: The abstract mentions a binary representation but does not define it; this is the natural choice.

equations.label: MCZ gate action
equations.description: A Z gate controlled on all other qubits in S applies a phase of -1 only when all qubits in S are 1.
equations.justification: Standard definition of multiple-controlled Z, which is symmetric in its qubits.

equations.label: Decomposition as GF(2) linear combination
equations.description: Decomposition is writing b(D) in the MCZ basis over GF(2). Diagonal gates commute and their phases add mod 2.
equations.abstract_quote: the problem of decomposing a given diagonal Hermitian gate is mapped to the problem of writing its binary representation in the specific basis mentioned above
equations.justification: Directly follows from the stated mapping, with the GF(2) field being an inference given the binary vectors.
assumptions: f(0)=0 so the global phase is +1 (otherwise a global -1 is needed)

equations.label: n=2 instance
equations.description: Triangular system solved by c_2=f(01), c_1=f(10), c_12=f(11)⊕f(01)⊕f(10).
equations.justification: Worked tiny instance of the mapping with an invertible basis matrix.

registers.name: q
registers.role: qubits on which the diagonal gate acts

steps.description: Given a diagonal Hermitian D, read off the signs d_x and form f(x) and b(D).
Solve the GF(2) linear system in the MCZ basis for the coefficients c_S.
Emit one MCZ_S gate for each S with c_S=1; for n=2 these are Z on qubit 1, Z on qubit 2, and CZ.

specification.classical_postprocessing: Solve the GF(2) linear system, with the matrix entries given by products of bits, to obtain the coefficients c_S.
assumptions: Chosen scope is the n=2 instance.
The binary representation is taken to be the f-vector, which may differ from the paper.
Global phase is ignored or f(0)=0.
missing_information: The paper's exact binary representation definition
Its cost model and the CZ versus CNOT library cost comparison
Any optimization of the gate ordering or synthesis of MCZ gates into CZ
